memory_annotations.evidence_summary: Marcus endorsed prioritizing a balcony when available for family coastal stays, while explicitly treating it as a soft preference and accepting a suitable first-floor room without one. This supports the supplied hotel-view-balcony-flexibility policy without introducing another durable preference.

messages.content: Price the actual hotels now. Use Friday June 20 through Friday June 27 as the main set, but check Saturday June 21 through Saturday June 28 too. I want one serious Mission Bay choice and one Coronado alternative, with the real total after fees, taxes, and parking.

I’ll compare rooms that explicitly allow two adults and one 12-year-old, not just rooms labeled for two. One date check first: both flight patterns produce seven hotel nights, not eight. Should I keep the search at seven nights to match the flights?
Yes, seven nights. That eight-night reference was wrong. Keep the flights exactly as they are.

For June 20-27, the strongest initial matches are Bahia Resort Hotel in Mission Bay and Coronado Island Marriott Resort & Spa. Both have rooms whose occupancy rules explicitly permit three guests. I’m checking room configuration, mandatory charges, parking, and the cancellation terms attached to the quoted rates now.
Good. Also compare the practical driving. We’ll have beach days, one zoo day, and the Disneyland day trip.

Bahia, Deluxe Bay View room: two queen beds, maximum occupancy four, private balcony, and no rollaway needed for three. Seven-night room subtotal is $2,688. Resort fee is $294, estimated lodging taxes are $378.52, and self-parking is $280. Complete stay total: $3,640.52. The refundable rate can be canceled through 6:00 p.m. local time on June 13; after that, the penalty is one night plus tax.
And the Coronado room? Make sure it is not a king room with a vague sofa-bed listing.

The comparable Coronado Island Marriott quote is a first-floor two-queen guest room with a terrace. It permits up to four guests, so two adults and Owen are covered without a sofa bed. Room subtotal is $2,856. The destination fee is $350, estimated lodging taxes are $449.68, and self-parking is $378. Complete total: $4,033.68. Cancellation is free through 11:59 p.m. local time on June 15; canceling later triggers a one-night room-and-tax charge.
Is that terrace effectively a balcony, or is it ground level?

It is ground level, not a balcony. The room opens to a furnished outdoor terrace. A two-queen room with an upper-floor balcony is available for the same dates, but its complete total with fees, taxes, and parking is $4,454.06, or $420.38 more.

For family coastal stays, prioritize a balcony when it’s available, but treat that as a soft preference. A first-floor room like this is acceptable without one, and I don’t want to eliminate an otherwise good hotel over it.

Understood. Bahia’s balcony room remains the direct fit. For Coronado, I’ll keep the first-floor terrace room in contention because the outdoor space is usable and the balcony upgrade is substantial, while noting the upper-floor option separately rather than making it the default quote.
Now give me the driving comparison. Use realistic ranges, not best-case estimates.

From Bahia, the hotel’s Mission Bay beach is on site, Mission Beach is usually 5-10 minutes, the San Diego Zoo about 15-25 minutes, and Disneyland roughly 90-120 minutes each way before unusual incidents. From Coronado Island Marriott, Coronado Beach is about 10-15 minutes, the zoo 15-25 minutes, Mission Beach 20-35 minutes, and Disneyland about 95-125 minutes. Coronado also adds bridge traffic exposure when going to most mainland activities.
So Bahia is $393.16 cheaper than the Coronado terrace room, correct?

Correct. $4,033.68 minus $3,640.52 is $393.16. Bahia also avoids repeated bridge crossings for the zoo and Mission Beach, while Coronado gives easier access to Coronado Beach and the island’s restaurants.
What happens to those same two rooms on the Saturday-to-Saturday flight fallback?

For June 21-28, Bahia’s same Deluxe Bay View two-queen balcony room totals $3,782.44: $2,814 room, $294 resort fee, $394.44 estimated tax, and $280 parking. Free cancellation runs through 6:00 p.m. June 14. The Coronado Marriott first-floor two-queen terrace room totals $3,918.70: $2,754 room, $350 destination fee, $436.70 estimated tax, and $378 parking. Free cancellation runs through 11:59 p.m. June 16.
Interesting. Add the airfare so I can see whether Saturday actually wins overall.

Friday pattern: $1,587 airfare plus $3,640.52 at Bahia equals $5,227.52; with Coronado it is $5,620.68. Saturday pattern: $1,536 airfare plus $3,782.44 at Bahia equals $5,318.44; with Coronado it is $5,454.70. Saturday is $90.92 more with Bahia, but $165.98 less with Coronado.
The Saturday United flight arrives in the morning, though. Does that create an extra hotel issue before check-in?

Yes. United arrives at 10:35 a.m., while standard check-in at both properties is 4:00 p.m. They can hold luggage, but early room access is not guaranteed. The Friday American flight arrives at 8:45 p.m., so the room should be ready, though the first night is mostly an arrival night. Neither quote includes guaranteed early check-in or late checkout.
Keep Friday as primary. The cleaner arrival and the cheaper Bahia combination are enough. Which property are you actually recommending?

Primary recommendation: Bahia Resort Hotel for June 20-27 in the Deluxe Bay View room with two queens and a private balcony. It explicitly accommodates all three of you, totals $3,640.52 including resort fee, estimated taxes, and seven nights of self-parking, and has the best logistics for repeated beach time plus the zoo. Cancel by 6:00 p.m. June 13 to avoid the one-night-plus-tax penalty.
And keep Coronado credible, not just as a throwaway. Restate exactly which room and why it survives.

Credible alternative: Coronado Island Marriott Resort & Spa, June 20-27, first-floor two-queen room with furnished terrace, maximum occupancy four. Complete total is $4,033.68 including the destination fee, estimated taxes, and self-parking. Cancel through 11:59 p.m. June 15 without penalty. It remains viable for stronger access to Coronado Beach and island dining; its tradeoffs are the $393.16 premium and more bridge-dependent driving. The upper-floor balcony version is available at $4,454.06, but the terrace room is the better-value alternative. Nothing has been booked.
